repos.name: CheatRunner
repos.readme:
CheatRunner

A web-based cheat trainer for your PlayStation 5!

--- **CheatRunner** runs as a single ELF on an already-jailbroken PS5 and serves its complete interface over HTTP. No desktop client is required. Send `CheatRunner.elf` to the console, open the PS5 IP address on port `9999` in a browser, and manage your games and cheats from a desktop, tablet, or smartphone. CheatRunner brings the most common PS5 trainer workflows together in one interface: - Browse installed games and apps, with covers, version, play time, and last played; - Launch installed titles from a browser; - Load local cheat files (`.mc4`, `.shn`, `.json`) and turn cheats on or off with one click; - Apply PS-Game-Patch XML patches; - Download cheat collections from community sources; - Re-apply your cheats and patches automatically when a game starts; - Open a game's trainer from a controller shortcut or the game's options menu; - Inspect logs and diagnostics. > **One payload. One dashboard. No companion application required.** --- ## ✨ Features - **Games library** — PS5 / PS4 / Apps filters, covers, title ID, version, time played, last played, and one-click launch. - **Favorites and Recent** — stored on the console, so every device that opens the dashboard sees the same lists. - **Full-page trainer** — per-game **Cheats**, **Patches** and **Files** tabs, a readiness strip, and the cheat and patch authors shown up front. - **Cheat formats** — `.mc4`, `.shn`, and `.json`; master-code and code-cave cheats of any size are supported. - **One-click cheats** — click to turn on, click again to turn off, with post-write verification and rollback. - **Version-aware selection** — exact version first, generic file as fallback, wrong version as a last resort with a visible warning. - **PS-Game-Patch XML patches** — version-aware (`AppVer`), with mask-version patches applied regardless of game version. - **Autoload profiles** — save the cheats and/or patches that are on; they are re-applied the next time the game launches, with an on-screen notification. - **Crash-suspect detection** — mods that crashed the game are flagged and blocked from re-enabling automatically. - **Controller shortcut and game menu** — hold two buttons (L2 + R3 by default) or pick **★ CheatRunner** in a game's options menu to open that game's trainer. - **Cheat sources** — download a whole repository as one archive with a live progress panel; unchanged files are skipped. - **16 Languages** — complete UI translation with RTL support for Arabic and Persian. - **Themes and visual effects** — five themes, plus a **Full** and a **Reduced** effects preset; Reduced is the default in the PS5 browser. - **Responsive interface** — designed for desktop, tablets, and smartphones. - **Phone access** — a QR code opens CheatRunner on your phone. - **Command palette** — quick keyboard navigation with `Ctrl/Cmd + K`. - **Logs and diagnostics** — a health summary, a Copy Logs button, and a per-session log file. - **Config hot-reload** — edits to `config.ini` over FTP/SSH are picked up automatically, no restart needed. - **Update notice** — shows a message when a newer GitHub release exists. --- ## 🚀 Getting Started ### Requirements CheatRunner is intended for a PS5 that already has a compatible jailbreak/homebrew environment running. You will need: - An already-jailbroken PlayStation 5; - A compatible ELF/payload loader; - A computer, phone, or tablet on the same local network as the console. ### Run CheatRunner Send: ```text CheatRunner.elf ``` to the PS5 using your preferred ELF loader. Then open the dashboard from another device on the same network: ```text http://:9999 ``` Example: ```text http://192.168.1.100:9999 ``` CheatRunner serves the complete frontend directly from the ELF. ### Homebrew Launcher CheatRunner also ships as a Homebrew Launcher package (`CheatRunner.zip`). 1. Extract the zip **directly into `/data/homebrew/`** on your PS5 via FTP. 2. Check that the result is: ```text /data/homebrew/CheatRunner/ ├── CheatRunner.elf ├── homebrew.js └── sce_sys/ └── icon0.png ``` 3. Open the Homebrew Launcher on your PS5, launch **CheatRunner**, then open the dashboard in your browser. --- ## 🔄 Updating CheatRunner **Before updating to a new version, please follow these steps:** 1. Go to `/data/cheatrunner` and delete **everything** except the `cheats` and `patches` folders. - Keep both folders — there is **no need** to delete them. - Do this **before** using the new version, **not after**. 2. Delete the old **CheatRunner PKG** (home-screen tile) from your PS5. 3. Clear your browser cache: **Settings → System → Browser → Clear Cache**. Then send the new `CheatRunner.elf` as usual. --- ## 🎮 Games & Trainer The **Games** page lists everything installed on the console, with the PS5 / PS4 / Apps filters, search, favorites, and recent titles. Each game card shows the title ID, a PS5/PS4 badge, version, time played, and last played, plus **Play** and **Trainer** actions. The trainer opens as a full page with three tabs: - **Cheats** — switches for every mod in the loaded cheat file; - **Patches** — the PS-Game-Patch entries that match the game and its version; - **Files** — the cheat files found for this title, with a selector to force another candidate. Cheat and patch authors are shown on the page and on each patch, so credit always stays visible. --- ## 🧰 Local Cheats CheatRunner is local-first. Local cheat files remain the primary workflow. ### Search paths (scanned in order) ```text /data/cheatrunner/cheats ← primary path /data/etaHEN/cheats ← etaHEN cross-compatibility /data/elf-arsenal/cheats ← elf-arsenal cross-compatibility ``` Recommended sub-folders inside the primary path: ```text /data/cheatrunner/cheats/mc4 /data/cheatrunner/cheats/shn /data/cheatrunner/cheats/json ``` Example files: ```text /data/cheatrunner/cheats/mc4/PPSA30803_01.200.000.mc4 /data/cheatrunner/cheats/mc4/PPSA30803.mc4 /data/cheatrunner/cheats/shn/CUSA00000.shn /data/cheatrunner/cheats/json/CUSA00000.json ``` ### Version-aware selection CheatRunner matches cheat files by title ID and game version: - **Exact match** (`CUSA00000_01.09.json`) — selected automatically when the running game reports that version. - **Generic** (`CUSA00000.json`, no version in the filename) — used as fallback when no exact match exists. - **Wrong version** — loaded as a last resort when no exact or generic file exists; the trainer shows a version-mismatch warning and a `WRONG VER` badge. The candidate selector lets you force-switch or download a better match. --- ## 🩹 Local Patches CheatRunner supports **PS-Game-Patch** XML patches. Patch search paths (scanned in this order): ```text /data/cheatrunner/patches/xml_prospero ← PS5-native patches /data/cheatrunner/patches/xml ← PS4 BC / general patches /data/elf-arsenal/patches/xml ← elf-arsenal cross-compatibility /data/cheatrunner/patches ← loose .xml files ``` Notes: - Sub-folders (such as a downloaded repo) are scanned too, and `.xml` is matched in any letter case. - Files need a `` block; ones without it are skipped and logged as `index_skip no_title_id`. - New files are picked up automatically, or press Refresh in the dashboard. - **CheatRunner Patches** are saved in `xml/cheatrunner` and `xml_prospero/cheatrunner`. If a game has patches there, only those are used and PS-Game-Patch files for the same game are ignored; games they don't cover keep using PS-Game-Patch. ### Patches that must be applied at game start Some patches only take effect if they are written in the first seconds of the game, because the game reads the value once at boot (for example the RDR2 60 FPS patch). Applying them while the game is already running writes the bytes but changes nothing. 1. Open the game and apply the patch from the **Patches** tab. 2. Click **Save autoload**. 3. Close the game and open it again. CheatRunner applies the patch on its own as soon as the game starts. --- ## 🌐 Sources The **Sources** page downloads community cheat and patch collections straight to the console: - HEN Cheats Collection (recommended); - PS5 Cheats; - GoldHEN Cheats; - HEN PPSA Cheats; - CheatRunner Patches (community patches released by the maintainer); - The official PS-Game-Patch release. Repositories are fetched as a single archive, with live progress, speed, and ETA. A download in progress also shows in the top bar on every page. By default, files that already exist are left untouched and only new files are added. Turn on **Also update files that changed** to refresh existing files with the repository's latest version; local-only files are never deleted. Keep it off if you edited a file by hand. --- ## 🔁 Autoload Profiles Autoload profiles re-apply your cheats and/or patches every time you launch a game — no need to open the dashboard and toggle them on again. **Important:** an autoload profile only saves the cheats/patches that are **currently ON/applied at the moment you save it**. It does not save the whole cheat or patch file. ### Cheats 1. Open a game's trainer and enable the cheats you want. 2. In the **Cheats** tab, click **Save Autoload Profile**. 3. Next time you launch that game, CheatRunner re-applies those cheats and shows an on-screen notification. 4. To stop, click **Clear Autoload Profile**. ### Patches 1. Open a game's trainer and apply the patches you want. 2. In the **Patches** tab, click **Save Autoload Profile**. 3. Next time you launch that game, CheatRunner re-applies those patches and shows an on-screen notification. 4. To stop, click **Clear Autoload Profile**. Cheat and patch profiles are independent — you can save one, both, or neither for any game. --- ## 🕹️ Controller Shortcut & Game Menu Off by default. Turn on **Controller shortcut and game menu** in Settings to: - hold the chosen two buttons (L2 + R3 by default) while a game is running to open its trainer; - get a **★ CheatRunner** entry in the game's options menu that opens that game's trainer. This works by hooking SceShellUI, so it needs a few seconds after boot or rest mode to arm. CheatRunner never restarts the system UI. If the console misbehaves, turn the option off in Settings and restart CheatRunner. --- ## 🎨 Look & Feel - **Themes** — five themes; Midnight (blue) is the default. - **Visual effects** — **Full** keeps blur, glow, and motion; **Reduced** turns them off for the PS5 browser. Reduced is chosen automatically on the PS5 until you pick Full in Settings. - **Phones and tablets** — the layout adapts down to small phone widths. Tip: keep the dashboard open on a PC or phone while playing. The PS5 browser competes with the game for resources. --- ## 🌍 Languages CheatRunner supports a fully localized interface in: - 🇺🇸 **English** - 🇸🇦 **Arabic** - 🇨🇳 **Chinese Simplified** - 🇫🇷 **French** - 🇩🇪 **German** - 🇮🇹 **Italian** - 🇯🇵 **Japanese** - 🇰🇷 **Korean** - 🇮🇷 **Persian** - 🇵🇱 **Polish** - 🇧🇷 **Brazilian Portuguese** - 🇷🇺 **Russian** - 🇪🇸 **Spanish** - 🇹🇭 **Thai** - 🇹🇷 **Turkish** - 🇺🇦 **Ukrainian** English is the default language. Arabic and Persian use RTL layouts, while technical values such as paths, URLs, title IDs, versions, and logs stay in their natural LTR form. --- ## 🧪 Notes & Bug Reports CheatRunner is still experimental. Some cheats may work correctly, fail to apply, mismatch the game version, crash the game, require a specific game update, or behave differently after relaunching the game. When reporting bugs, include: - CheatRunner logs (Copy Logs button, or `/data/cheatrunner/logs.txt`); - the game title ID and version/update; - the cheat file used; - which cheat was enabled or disabled; - what happened before the issue. Each log session starts with a header line, and the log level is `debug` by default. --- ## ⚠️ Disclaimer CheatRunner is **not a jailbreak**, **not an exploit**, and **not a tool for stock/retail consoles**. It only works when your PS5 is already jailbroken and already has the required homebrew/payload environment running. CheatRunner does **not** provide: - jailbreaks or kernel exploits; - game backups or game content; - piracy features; - PSN bypasses; - online services. It is a local homebrew tool for testing trainers on your own already-jailbroken console. Runtime cheat memory writes can crash the game, break a session, corrupt your savegame, softlock the title, or behave differently depending on the game version/update. **Always back up your save files before using any cheats.** Use CheatRunner at your own risk. --- ## 🛠️ Building CheatRunner is built with the **PS5 Payload SDK** and a plain `Makefile`. On Windows, build inside WSL. You need the SDK, `make` and `python3` (the dashboard, i18n, and payload blobs are generated at build time), plus a host C compiler (used to pre-compress the dashboard). ```sh make # writes build-make/CheatRunner.elf make clean ``` `./build-cheatrunner.sh` wraps `make` with a tool check, a single progress line and a build summary (size, SHA-256, time): ```sh ./build-cheatrunner.sh # normal build ./build-cheatrunner.sh --clean -j 4 # wipe build-make/ first, 4 parallel jobs ./build-cheatrunner.sh --verbose # full make output ./build-cheatrunner.sh --help # all options (--sqlite, --no-sqlite, --skip-js-check) ``` Each log session starts with a short build id, so reports say which ELF was running. The Makefile looks for the SDK in this order: ```text 1. /opt/ps5-payload-sdk 2. PS5_PAYLOAD_SDK environment variable 3. ./PS5-Projects/sdk-master 4. ./ps5-payload-sdk ``` SQLite: if `src/third_party/sqlite3.c` and `sqlite3.h` exist, bundled SQLite is enabled automatically. Use `make SQLITE=1` to force it on and `make SQLITE=0` to disable it. Output: ```text build-make/CheatRunner.elf ``` --- ## 📁 Repository Layout ```text . ├── build-make/ Build output ├── pkg-source/ PS5 home-screen tile sources ├── src/ │ ├── web/ Dashboard (HTML, CSS, vanilla JS, locales) │ ├── payload/ Code injected into SceShellUI │ └── third_party/ Bundled libraries ├── tools/ Build and validation scripts ├── Makefile └── build-cheatrunner.sh ``` The dashboard is written as plain files in `src/web/`; `make` compresses and embeds it directly into `CheatRunner.elf`. --- ## ❤️ Support CheatRunner is free and open-source. If you find it useful, consider supporting further development. **PIX - Brazilian method** **LivePix**: https://livepix.gg/notmaj0r **Donate via Crypto** - **BTC** `bc1ppfcad9ytyzmmzq3nfatfcag7q38rqcpsvxfqusq0uzv4gh82pa4syeknlk` - **BCH (Bitcoin Cash)** `qz2h97c2pyexn3fwhveu33tn5xkd3qlfn5796zhtcq` - **USDC (Solana)** `BNpezXSQWuUR9HWGjzQUS7AeEBCwiY2ZGxArWNwYXKKV` - **USDT (TON)** `UQA18f4cVS0778fL_nIssdN1GIHRYR7dQ3UnNgjPwgYvIQi_` --- ## 🤝 Credits & References CheatRunner exists thanks to the PS4/PS5 homebrew and research community. - **ELF Arsenal & VoidShell** — for project ideas and implementations. - **[Ps5-Payload-Dev](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev)** — for the [SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) CheatRunner is built with. - **[etaHEN](https://github.com/etaHEN/etaHEN)** (LightningMods) and **[onionHEN](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN)** (aydencharles) — the SceShellUI injection and hooking approach behind the controller shortcut and the ★ CheatRunner game-menu entry is adapted from their work. - **miniz** (Rich Geldreich) and **[qrcode-generator](https://github.com/kazuhikoarase/qrcode-generator)** (Kazuhiko Arase) — bundled libraries used for unpacking cheat archives and the QR code. - **TeeKay87** — for the [HEN-Cheats-Collection](https://github.com/TeeKay87/HEN-Cheats-Collection) project. - **etaHEN** — for the [PS5_Cheats](https://github.com/etaHEN/PS5_Cheats) project. - **GoldHEN** — for the [GoldHEN_Cheat_Repository](https://github.com/GoldHEN/GoldHEN_Cheat_Repository) project. - **RDX-Sci01** — for the [HEN-PPSA-Cheats](https://github.com/RDX-Sci01/HEN-PPSA-Cheats) project. - **illusionyy** — for the [PS-Game-Patch](https://github.com/illusionyy/ps-game-patch) and [ps-patch-system](https://github.com/illusionyy/ps-patch-system) projects. - Everyone testing, reporting issues, sharing logs, and helping improve the project. --- ## 📜 License CheatRunner is licensed under the **GNU General Public License v3.0**. See the `LICENSE` file for the full license text. ```text GNU General Public License v3.0 ``` ---

repos.name: kylin-core-release
repos.readme:
Kylin Core
A homebrew cheat loader and real-time game modifier for PlayStation 5

English · 简体中文

Features · Run · Cheat files · Web UI · Runtime data · Troubleshooting · Support · Credits

---

Kylin Core ships as a single ELF. The payload boots a background daemon,
registers its own home-screen tile, detects the running title, patches game
memory on demand, and serves a local web UI on port 9023.


# Features Kylin Core is a single-payload cheat tool for jailbroken PS5 consoles. It runs as a persistent daemon instead of a one-shot loader. - **Real-time cheat toggle** — enable or disable a cheat while the game is running; the patch is applied or reverted immediately - **Automatic game detection** — the daemon resolves the running title by itself, so no manual title ID is needed - **Four cheat formats** — `.json`, `.shn`, `.mc4`, and `.ShnExt` (Alpha), all loaded from a single flat directory - **Hot reload** — cheat file edits apply immediately, with no restart - **Built-in web UI** — served straight from the payload on port `9023` and opened by the home-screen tile - **Home-screen tile** — the tile is registered automatically under the **Media** section of the home screen - **Game media** — the UI streams the installed title's icon and hero art through the daemon - **System notifications** — the daemon reports startup, ready, stop, and game launch through PS5 notifications - **Single-tool distribution** — no `ps5debug-NG`, no extra modules, no additional runtime dependencies - **Stable in-game operation** — no freeze on APR-protected titles The web UI is localized in **简体中文**, **English**, and **한국어**.
# Run ### Requirements 1. A jailbroken PS5 with a working ELF loader 2. [PS5 Payload Manager (PLDMGR)](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager) installed on the console ### Install 1. Load `kylin-core.elf` with **PS5 Payload Manager (PLDMGR)**. 2. Wait for the ready notification. The **Kylin Core** tile is under **Media** on the home screen. 3. Launch **Kylin Core** from the home screen. > [!IMPORTANT] > Load `kylin-core.elf` through PLDMGR **before** opening the tile. The tile is > only a browser launcher pointing at `http://127.0.0.1:9023/`; if the daemon is > not running, the UI has nothing to load. ### Compatibility | Target | Status | | --- | --- | | PS4 games running on PS5 | Supported | | PS5 native games | Supported | | PS5 games with APR | Supported | | Firmware | Jailbroken consoles on **4.0.3 through 13.60** | | Cheat formats | `.json` · `.shn` · `.mc4` · `.ShnExt` (Alpha) |
# Cheat files Cheat files live in one directory and follow one naming rule: ```text /data/kylin/cheats/_.json /data/kylin/cheats/_.shn /data/kylin/cheats/_.mc4 /data/kylin/cheats/_.ShnExt ``` - The directory is flat. Subfolders are not scanned. - `` is the running title's ID, for example `PPSA00001`. - `` is the running title's version with anything outside `0-9`, `A-Z`, `a-z`, `.`, `_`, and `-` replaced by `_`, so a version of `01.000.000` stays `01.000.000`. - One file is resolved per title, in the order `.json` → `.shn` → `.mc4` → `.ShnExt`. The first match wins, so a `.json` file shadows an `.shn` file for the same title and version. Editing a cheat file takes effect right away, even mid-session — no restart. > [!NOTE] > `.ShnExt` support is Alpha and not fully supported yet. `.json`, `.shn`, and > `.mc4` are the fully supported formats.
# Web UI The daemon serves its own frontend, embedded in the ELF. ```text http://127.0.0.1:9023/ on the console (what the launcher tile opens) http://:9023/ from any device on the same network ``` | Page | What it does | | --- | --- | | Cheats | Lists the running title and its cheats; toggles them individually | | Game | Shows the detected title, its icon and hero art, and the resolved cheat file | | Profile | Current user and avatar | | Settings | UI language and theme | | Logs | Reads and downloads the daemon log | The UI can also be pointed at a console manually from its connect screen, which is how it is used when served from a development build rather than from the daemon.
# Runtime data | Path | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `/data/kylin/` | Daemon data root, created on startup | | `/data/kylin/cheats/` | Cheat files, flat directory | | `/data/kylin/logs/kylin-core.log` | Daemon log, rotated at 256 KiB with 3 files kept | | `/tmp/kylin-core.log` | Log fallback used when the data root is not writable |
# Repository layout ```text . ├── assets/ Project artwork and screenshots ├── guide/ Installation guide ├── zh/ Simplified Chinese README and installation guide ├── LICENSE └── README.md ```
# Troubleshooting 1. **The tile opens a blank page or a browser error.** The daemon is not running. Load `kylin-core.elf` through PLDMGR first, wait for the ready notification, then reopen the tile. 2. **There is no Kylin Core tile on the home screen.** The tile is registered automatically when the payload starts. Confirm the payload reached the ready state, then check `/data/kylin/logs/kylin-core.log`. 3. **The daemon never becomes ready.** Confirm the payload matches your firmware and that PLDMGR reported a successful load. Check `/data/kylin/logs/kylin-core.log`, or `/tmp/kylin-core.log` if the data root was not writable. 4. **No game is detected.** Start the game first and let it reach the main menu, then refresh the Cheats page. The daemon only reports titles that are actually running. 5. **The cheat list is empty.** Check the filename. It must be `_.json`, `.shn`, `.mc4`, or `.ShnExt`, directly inside `/data/kylin/cheats` with no subfolder. 6. **A cheat is listed but does nothing.** Cheats are only as good as their implementation, and some depend on a specific game version. Verify the version segment of the filename against the running title. When reporting a problem, include the firmware version, the game title ID and version, the daemon log, and the steps that reproduce it.
# Support If Kylin Core is useful to you, consider supporting its continued development. Thank you.
# Credits Kylin Core exists because of the PS5 homebrew and reverse-engineering community. ### Used or embedded - [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) — Prospero toolchain, target headers, and runtime used to build the payload - [PS5 Payload Manager (PLDMGR)](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager) — itsplk; the ELF loader used to send the payload to the console; not shipped in the release - [CivetWeb](https://github.com/civetweb/civetweb) — the embedded web server that serves the UI - [cJSON](https://github.com/DaveGamble/cJSON) — JSON parsing and serialization - MC4 helper subset — `base64.c` carries a BSD notice by Jouni Malinen; `aes.c` is derived from [tiny-AES-c](https://github.com/kokke/tiny-AES-c) by kokke - [miniz](https://github.com/richgel999/miniz) — deflate and archive handling - [SHA-256](https://github.com/B-Con/crypto-algorithms) — Brad Conte; hashing used by the daemon - [Keystone](https://github.com/keystone-engine/keystone) — assembler used by the cheat engine
# License This project is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). Third-party components retain their respective licenses and notices. > Kylin Core is an unofficial homebrew project and is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment. > Use it only on hardware you own and at your own risk. No warranty is provided.

latestRelease.body: # Kylin Core v2.0.0 Community Lite If you find this project helpful, please consider supporting its continued development. Your support is greatly appreciated! ## 🎮 Features - **Real-time cheat toggle** — enable or disable cheats anytime during gameplay, changes apply instantly - **Multi-format support** — `.json` / `.shn` / `.mc4` / `.ShnExt` cheat files, all from a single flat directory (`.ShnExt` is Alpha) - **Automatic game detection** — no manual title ID needed - **Built-in web UI** — served by the payload itself and opened from the home-screen tile - **Cheat credits** — author names are read from the cheat file and shown on the game page - **Self-recovering service** — comes back on its own after rest mode or a network change - **Stable in-game operation** — no freeze on APR games ## 📦 Files | File | Description | Size | |---|---|---| | `kylin-core.elf` | The whole distribution: daemon, cheat engine and web UI | 4.8 MB | ## 🚀 Installation 1. Load `kylin-core.elf` via [PLDMGR](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager) 2. Wait for the ready notification. The **Kylin Core** tile is under **Media** on the home screen 3. Launch **Kylin Core** from the home screen > ⚠️ Load `kylin-core.elf` before opening the tile, otherwise the UI has nothing to load. 📖 **Full installation guide:** [guide/installation.md](https://github.com/aydencharles/kylin-core-release/blob/main/guide/installation.md) ## 📋 Compatibility - PS4 games (running on PS5): ✅ Supported - PS5 native games: ✅ Supported - PS5 games with APR: ✅ Supported - Firmware: **4.0.3 – 13.60** - Cheat formats: `.json` · `.shn` · `.mc4` · `.ShnExt` (Alpha — not fully supported yet) > [!NOTE] > `.ShnExt` support is Alpha. `.json`, `.shn` and `.mc4` are the fully supported formats. ## 📁 Cheat Directory Place cheat files in `/data/kylin/cheats` (flat directory only, no subfolders). ## 📝 Changelog ### Distribution - The release is a single ELF. repos.description: Common FPS for PS5 v1.0.0  First public stable release.  Universal real-time FPS overlay for PS4 and PS5 games on PS5.  This release includes both a standalone ELF and an etaHEN plugin.
repos.readme:
# Common FPS for PS5 v1.2.1

Real-time FPS overlay for PS4 and PS5 games on a modified PlayStation 5.

Common FPS displays the current frame rate directly over the game and is
available as a standalone ELF or etaHEN plugin.

## Features

- real-time integer FPS for PS4 and PS5 games;
- compact bottom-left overlay;
- purple `FPS:` label and white FPS value;
- 24px default font;
- `FPS: Loading` while the FPS source is being prepared;
- VideoOut sampling with adaptive `/dev/dce` fallback;
- no game-memory writes from the FPS sampler;
- automatic game PID reattachment;
- automatic ShellUI PID recovery;
- Rest Mode recovery on tested firmware;
- standalone ELF and etaHEN plugin builds;
- automated source build and artifact verification.

## Firmware status

| System software | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **4.51** | **Confirmed** | PS4 + PS5 games, 30/60 FPS, game switching, Rest Mode recovery, normal reboot |
| **9.00** | **Confirmed** | Shadow of the Colossus and Spider-Man 2 tested; FPS survives Rest Mode |
| **9.60** | **Confirmed baseline** | Existing hardware-tested FPS and lifecycle path |
| **7.60** | Test pending | Current v1.2.1 build needs a fresh hardware regression test |
| **10.xx** | Experimental | Code path exists, but hardware validation is still required |

A code path being present does not mean every firmware revision has been
physically tested. Confirmed and experimental status are kept separate.

## Download

Use **one** of these two files from the latest GitHub Release:

```text
Common_FPS_PS5_v1.2.1.elf
Common_FPS_PS5_etaHEN_v1.2.1.plugin
```

**Do not run the standalone ELF and etaHEN plugin at the same time.**

Latest release:

https://github.com/porhe911/Common-FPS-for-PS5/releases/latest

## Installation

### Standalone ELF

1. Start your jailbreak/etaHEN environment.
2. Send `Common_FPS_PS5_v1.2.1.elf` with your preferred payload launcher.
3. Start a PS4 or PS5 game.
4. The overlay appears automatically after the game and ShellUI readiness
   checks complete.

### etaHEN plugin

1. Install `Common_FPS_PS5_etaHEN_v1.2.1.plugin` through etaHEN's plugin
   system.
2. Enable the plugin/autoload option.
3. Start a game.
4. Common FPS waits for a stable game process before creating the overlay.

The plugin is the recommended option for persistent use.

## What's new in v1.2.1

FW 9.00 required a different ShellUI write path than the one used by earlier
tested firmware. Reading the target JIT code through MDBG worked, but the
verified one-byte UI-thread guard could not be written while the page remained
RX.

v1.2.1 adds a FW 9.00-specific safe transaction:

- ShellUI is stopped;
- expected bytes are verified;
- the target 16 KiB JIT page is temporarily changed from RX to RWX;
- only the required one-byte guard is written;
- the page is restored to RX immediately;
- the result is read back and verified;
- auth state is restored before the transaction completes.

No game-process write path was added.

## How FPS is measured

Common FPS prefers a validated VideoOut counter associated with the active
game. If that counter cannot be resolved safely, it falls back to the PS5
display controller through `/dev/dce`.

The DCE path:

- does not depend on per-game hardcoded offsets;
- does not write to game memory;
- can automatically identify a stable display-like counter;
- is confirmed on FW 4.51 and FW 9.00.

When DCE is healthy, expensive VideoOut discovery uses a 60-second backoff.
If DCE stops producing valid samples, VideoOut recovery is allowed again.

## Overlay

Default appearance:

```text
Position: bottom-left
Font size: 24
FPS: label: purple
FPS value: white
Format: integer only
```

## Rest Mode and recovery

Common FPS tracks both the active game process and `SceShellUI`.

When a game or ShellUI PID changes, the old state is discarded and the
required sampler/renderer components are brought up again.

Rest Mode recovery is hardware-confirmed on FW 4.51 and FW 9.00.

## Logs

Controller:

```text
/data/CommonFPS_v1_2_1.log
```

ShellUI:

```text
/data/CommonFPS_v1_2_1_shellui.log
```

If the overlay shows `FPS: Loading`, the controller log is the first file to
check.

## Build from source

GitHub Actions runs:

- **Host Source Tests**
- **PS5 Source Build**

The PS5 build produces:

```text
Common_FPS_PS5_v1.2.1.elf
Common_FPS_PS5_etaHEN_v1.2.1.plugin
Common_FPS_ShellUI_v1.2.1.elf
SHA256SUMS.txt
```

## License

Common FPS-owned source is licensed under **GPL-3.0-or-later**.

Homebrew software for modified PlayStation 5 systems. Use at your own risk.

repos.name: ps5-new-overlay
repos.readme: # PS5 Hardware Overlay 🎮 Легковесный автономный оверлей мониторинга температур и нагрузки для взломанной PlayStation 5 (поддержка FW 1.xx - 10.xx+). [English](#english) | [Русский](#русский) --- ## Русский Специализированное легковесное решение для мониторинга аппаратных показателей PlayStation 5 в реальном времени. В отличие от громоздких наборов вроде onionHEN / etaHEN, данный проект сфокусирован **исключительно на функции оверлея**: он не содержит лишних инструментов, читов, FTP-серверов или тяжелых зависимостей и не рискует вызвать панику ядра на высоких прошивках (включая FW 10.20). ### Основные возможности - ⚡ **Аппаратный счётчик кадров (FPS Counter)**: Замер реальной частоты вертикальной синхронизации и смены кадров дисплея через Display Controller Engine (`/dev/dce`) или секлок OnionHEN (`/system_tmp/fps_sample`). - 🖥️ **Нативный экранный оверлей (In-Game HUD)**: Настоящая полоса мониторинга, отрисовываемая прямо поверх игр через внедрение в `SceShellUI` (с активным `kstuff`). - 🎨 **Цветовая дифференциация метрик**: - **FPS**: золотисто-жёлтый (`#FFEB3B`) - **CPU**: зеленый (`#66FF66`) - **GPU**: фиолетовый (`#B366FF`) - **RAM**: оранжевый (`#FFB34D`) - **FAN**: бирюзовый (`#33E0FF`) - 🔕 **Без спама уведомлениями**: Постоянно всплывающие тосты отключены по умолчанию, чтобы не мешать погружению в игру. - 🌡️ **Температура CPU & GPU (SoC)**: Прямое чтение сенсоров в реальном времени (°C). - 💾 **Использование RAM & VRAM**: Объем занятой системной и видеопамяти. - 🌀 **Обороты кулера (Fan Duty)**: Скорость вращения вентилятора в процентах. - ⚙️ **Гибкая конфигурация**: Настройка через файл `/data/ps5_overlay/config.ini`. --- ### Отображение в играх - **Наэкранный HUD в играх (SceShellUI)**: - Внедряется автоматически в системный процесс `SceShellUI`. - В верхней части экрана во время любой игры отображается аккуратная полупрозрачная плашка с цветными показателями: ```text FPS: 60 | CPU: 58°C | GPU: 61°C | RAM: 4.8 GB | FAN: 35% ``` --- ### Быстрый старт #### Вариант 1: Запуск через ELF Loader (Port 9020 / 9021) После активации джейлбрейка отправьте скомпилированный `.elf` на консоль: ```bash # Через Netcat на порт 9020 (или 9021): nc -w 3 9020 < ps5_overlay.elf ``` или воспользуйтесь любой программой для отправки пейлоадов (PS5 Payload Sender / Netcat GUI). #### Вариант 2: Автозапуск через менеджер пейлоадов Скопируйте `ps5_overlay.elf` в директорию пейлоадов на консоли: ```text /data/OnionHEN/payloads/ps5_overlay.elf # или /data/etaHEN/payloads/ps5_overlay.elf ``` и включите автозапуск в меню консоли. --- ### Настройка (`config.ini`) Файл конфигурации можно разместить по пути: ```text /data/ps5_overlay/config.ini ``` Пример настроек (`config.ini.example`): ```ini [ps5_overlay] enabled = true show_fps = true ; Счётчик FPS (Hardware DCE / OnionHEN) show_cpu_temp = true ; Температура CPU show_cpu_load = true ; Загрузка CPU % show_all_cores = false ; Нагрузка по ядрам show_gpu_temp = true ; Температура GPU (SOC) show_gpu_load = true ; Загрузка VRAM % show_ram = true ; Использование RAM show_fan = true ; Обороты кулера % interval_ms = 1000 ; Опрос сенсоров (мс) toast_notifications = false ; Экранный OSD в играх (true/false) toast_interval_sec = 10 ; Интервал обновления OSD (сек) ``` --- ## English A lightweight, standalone hardware monitoring overlay for jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles (FW 1.xx - 10.xx+). Unlike full HEN suites (like onionHEN or etaHEN), this project focuses **exclusively on the overlay experience**: minimal footprint, zero bloat, no cheats, and no risk of kernel panics on newer firmwares (including FW 10.20). ### Features - ⚡ **Real-Time In-Game FPS Counter**: Accurate framerate monitoring sampled via Display Controller Engine (`/dev/dce`) hardware flip deltas or OnionHEN seqlock sampler (`/system_tmp/fps_sample`). - 🖥️ **Native In-Game HUD**: Translucent top-screen status bar rendered seamlessly over active gameplay via Mono PUI in `SceShellUI`. - 🌡️ **CPU Temperature**: Real-time reading of internal Zen 2 CPU sensors. - 🎯 **CPU Utilization**: Accurate CPU load percentage and 8-core tracks. - 🔥 **GPU / SoC Temperature**: APU / SoC thermal monitoring. - 🎮 **VRAM Usage**: Video memory usage percentage and MB. - 💾 **System RAM**: Memory footprint in GB and percentage (`4.8 / 16.0 GB`). - 🌀 **Fan Duty Cycle**: Real-time cooling fan speed percentage. - 🔕 **Zero Toast Spam**: Notification popups disabled by default to protect gameplay immersion. - ⚙️ **Configurable**: Managed via `/data/ps5_overlay/config.ini`. --- ## Сборка и GitHub Releases Проект настроен для автоматической компиляции и выпуска релизов через **GitHub Actions**: 1. **Автоматическая сборка**: При каждом коммите в ветку `main` GitHub Actions собирает `ps5_overlay.elf` с помощью актуального `ps5-payload-sdk` и сохраняет артефакты. 2. **Публикация релиза**: - При создании тега версии: ```bash git tag v1.0.1 git push origin v1.0.1 ``` - Или вручную через вкладку **Actions** -> **Build and Release PS5 Overlay** -> **Run workflow**. GitHub Action автоматически скомпилирует бинарный файл, сгенерирует `SHA256SUMS.txt` и прикрепит их к новому релизу в разделе **Releases**. --- ## Лицензия Распространяется под лицензией MIT / GPLv3. Отдельная благодарность разработчикам `ps5-payload-dev`, `etaHEN` и сообществу сцены PS5.

latestRelease.name: PS5 Hardware Overlay v1.0.15
latestRelease.body:
## 🎮 PS5 Hardware Overlay v1.0.15

Lightweight, standalone in-game hardware monitoring overlay for jailbroken PlayStation 5 (FW 1.xx - 10.xx+, kstuff active).

### ✨ What's New in v1.0.15
- **🧹 Streamlined Architecture (Pure In-Game Overlay)**:
  - Completely removed embedded HTTP web server, sockets, and heavy HTML template assets.
  - Minimal footprint, zero background network listening, and maximum stability.
- **⚡ Real-Time In-Game FPS Counter**:
  - Hardware scanout flip delta sampling via Display Controller Engine (`/dev/dce`, `ioctl 0x80308217`).
  - Native fallback support for OnionHEN seqlock sampler (`/system_tmp/fps_sample`).
  - Dedicated **FPS** badge in gold/yellow (`#FFEB3B`) with live framerate (`60` / `120` / `--`).
  - Configurable via `show_fps = true` in `/data/ps5_overlay/config.ini`.
- **🖥️ Native On-Screen In-Game HUD**:
  - Automatically injected into `SceShellUI` via `ptrace` (with `kstuff` active).
  - Rendered directly on top of gameplay via Mono PUI (`Scene.RootWidget`).
  - Sleek translucent 2D bar at top of screen with color-coded metrics:
    - **FPS** (Gold/Yellow `#FFEB3B`)
    - **CPU** (Green `#66FF66`)
    - **GPU** (Purple `#B366FF`)
    - **RAM** (Orange `#FFB34D`)
    - **FAN** (Cyan `#33E0FF`)
- **🔕 Zero Toast Spam**:
  - Recurring notification popups completely disabled to protect your gameplay immersion.
  - Only a single silent startup toast confirms the overlay is loaded.

### 🚀 Quick Start
1. Ensure **kstuff** is active on your PS5.
2. Send `ps5_overlay.elf` to your console via port **9020** or **9021**:
   ```bash
   nc -w 3 <ps5_ip> 9020 < ps5_overlay.elf
   ```
3. A single notification appears confirming the overlay is active.
4. Launch any game — the hardware HUD bar appears at the top of the screen!

### 🔒 SHA-256 Checksums
Included in `SHA256SUMS.txt`.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/smoxa/ps5-new-overlay/compare/v1.0.14...v1.0.15
